review_notes: Read the whole target file. Checked Torus.unitCell_ae_eq_unitCube and integral_unitCell_eq_unitCube in Infra/Torus/Basic.lean, and how neighbouring files handle the cell-versus-cube measure comparison. I did not check the MemL2On definition. I flagged only changes that remove dead or repeated steps, and I did not flag shortenings that would hurt readability. Nothing was compiled, so the replacements are untested. The new helper lemma name is a proposal, not an existing lemma.

findings.problem: `hcellLe` is never used. The final `exact` uses only `hcubeLe`. The two-sided comparison is built by hand with `restrict_mono_ae`, although the codebase already has `Measure.restrict_congr_set` for exactly this a.e.-equal-sets rewrite.
findings.proposed_change:
Delete `hcellLe`. Replace lines 121–124 with the codebase's usual idiom:
```lean
  rw [Measure.restrict_congr_set AVenhance.Infra.Torus.unitCell_ae_eq_unitCube] at hbase
  exact hbase
```
If `MemL2On` does not unfold under `exact`, keep one inequality and write `exact hbase.mono_measure (Measure.restrict_mono_ae AVenhance.Infra.Torus.unitCell_ae_eq_unitCube.ge)`.
findings.benefit: This removes an unused hypothesis and about six lines. The last step then reads as one fact: the open cell and the closed cube differ by a null set. It also matches the idiom used elsewhere in the code.

findings.excerpt:
have hfun : weakPathRepresentative u t = scalarTorusRepresentative (u t) := by
    funext x
    simp [weakPathRepresentative, t.property]
findings.problem: The same unfolding proof, `funext x; simp [weakPathRepresentative, ...]`, is repeated in four places. These are `isPeriodic` (lines 156–158), `memL2On` (171–173), `l2NormSq` (180–182) and `htheta`'s `hrep` (200–202). The `isPeriodic` case also repeats it for the out-of-range branch. Each time the reader re-checks the same dite-unfolding fact.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the unfolding fact once, right after the definition:
```lean
theorem weakPathRepresentative_of_mem (u : Icc (0:ℝ) 1 → ScalarTorusL2) (t : Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    weakPathRepresentative u t = scalarTorusRepresentative (u t) := by
  funext x; simp [weakPathRepresentative, t.property]
```
Then `weakPathRepresentative_memL2On` becomes `by rw [weakPathRepresentative_of_mem]; exact scalarTorusRepresentative_memL2On (u t)`. `weakPathRepresentative_l2NormSq` and `hrep` in the pairing lemma shrink in the same way. In `isPeriodic`, the in-range branch can use `⟨t, ht⟩` with this lemma.
findings.benefit: This gives one named, reusable statement of what the representative is at an in-range time. Each downstream proof becomes a rewrite plus the corresponding `scalarTorusRepresentative_*` lemma, which makes the intent clearer and removes about 10 duplicated lines.
